tactical_rationale: No edge exists and the board proves it structurally. Every genuine partition carries a positive overround: the tightest is Odd/Even at 1.052486 (5.25pct), then 1X2 at 1.057692 (5.77pct), 2H 1X2 1.068389, 1H 1X2 1.075093, 1X2&O/U 1.163411, HT/FT 1.219818, Correct Score 1.254841. Cross-family covers cannot beat this because the derived markets are generated from the same scoreline model with an additional margin rather than from an independent price: 1X2 plus the complementary Double Chance leg reconciles exactly to p_sum 1.000 with implied sums of 1.056-1.070, so the DC leg adds 0.2-1.3pct of extra vig instead of removing any. Validation: SportyBet's own de-vigged probability field on 1X2 (0.2878/0.3139/0.3983) matches our Shin solution (0.2891/0.3144/0.3965) within 0.2pct, confirming one internal model with no leakage between tabs. Three apparent sub-1.0 combinations are structural traps, not arbs: (1) '1X2 Never Down' books 3.53/3.00/2.60 for a 1.0012 sum, but its Home/Away legs are 'never trailed' subsets of an ordinary win, both cash on 0-0, and come-from-behind wins cash nothing, so the 0.12pct is a ~6pct margin on a sub-1 probability base; (2) 1x2 Draw @3.00 plus 'Away No Bet: Draw' @1.76 sums to 0.8759, but Away No Bet voids on an away win, so an away victory loses the Home leg and refunds the other, a total loss; (3) 1x2 Draw @3.00 plus BTTS No @1.74 sums to 0.9080, but the union covers only 0.7257 of the outcome space (2-1/3-1/1-2/1-3 type results pay neither). Best achievable guaranteed return on any true cover is 0.9470 per unit (Odd/Even), a 5.3pct loss. The book is efficiently margined across all 215 markets; no superedge.
